transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve been hearing voices… mostly in my apartment. Sometimes in empty rooms at the museum too. They sound like women whispering behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive.
Do the voices ever tell you to do something or influence your actions in any way?
Yes… sort of. They tell me which photographs belong in the archive. It sounds like women whispering behind the walls, and I… I do find myself paying attention to it.
Do the voices ever directly tell you to do something, like an action you must take?
They don’t say it like “you must,” exactly. It’s more… they whisper which photographs belong in the archive, and I feel like I’m supposed to listen.
Do you ever feel like the voices are ordering you to do something, even if it's not in a direct command?

Yes… I suppose it feels that way sometimes. Not like they shout orders, but the voices are clear, like women behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive. I end up feeling like I’m meant to follow that.
Are the voices something you hear all the time or do they come and go?
They come and go. It’s not every minute… but it happens a lot in my apartment, and sometimes in empty museum rooms. Clear voices, like women whispering behind the walls.
Do the voices cause you any distress or anxiety?
Yes… it does. I get anxious when it’s clear like that, in my apartment especially. The whispering behind the walls… about the photographs and the archive. It’s hard to settle after.
Do you believe the voices you hear are real, or do you think they might be a product of your own mind?
I… it feels real when it’s happening. Like they’re actually behind the walls, whispering about the photographs. Later I can wonder if it’s my mind, but in the moment it doesn’t feel that way.
Do you ever find it hard to keep your thoughts straight or express them in a way that makes sense to others?

Sometimes, yes. My cousin will ask me something simple… like about a bill, or an appointment, and I’ll start answering, but then I’m talking about the grant, or shipping routes, or my grandmother’s altar. And then I can see they don’t know what I meant.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when talking or thinking?

Yes… I think so. If my cousin asks something simple, like a bill or an appointment, I’ll start answering and then I’m on about the grant, then shipping routes, then my grandmother’s altar. By the time I stop, people look like they don’t know what I meant.
Do you find that your way of thinking or expressing ideas is confusing to others most of the time?

I guess… not all the time, but it happens enough. Like I’ll mean to answer something simple, a bill or an appointment, and then I’m talking about the grant, or shipping routes, or my grandmother’s altar. People look lost by the end.
Do you find that your thoughts are often disorganized or hard to follow for most of the day?

Most of the day… I don’t know. It happens a lot, though. Like I said, my cousin asks about a bill or an appointment, and I start with that, then I’m on the grant, and shipping routes, and my grandmother’s altar. By the end, nobody seems to know what I meant.
Do you think your way of thinking is more disorganized than other people's most of the time?

Probably, yes. I don’t always notice it, but… people seem to get lost when I talk. Like with my cousin, I start on a bill or appointment and end up on the grant, shipping routes, my grandmother’s altar… and then nobody knows what I meant.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of sadness, depression, or elevated mood?

Yes… sometimes my mood goes very high. I feel almost radiant, like I’ve been chosen for something. But if someone questions what I’m doing or tells me to slow down, I can get… really angry. Like they’re trying to erase me.
Is your thinking usually disorganized like this, even when you're not hearing the voices?

Yes… I think so. Even when it’s quiet, I can still get tangled up. Like my cousin asks about a bill or an appointment, and I start somewhere else—about the grant, then shipping routes, then my grandmother’s altar. And by the end… people don’t seem to know what I was trying to say.
Is your thinking usually disorganized, even when you're not feeling anxious or hearing the voices?

Yes… even when I’m not anxious or hearing anything. It still happens. My cousin can ask one simple thing, like about a bill or an appointment, and I’ll start talking about the grant, then shipping routes, then my grandmother’s altar… and then I can see nobody knows what I meant.
Is your thinking usually disorganized even when you're feeling calm and not hearing any voices?

Yes… I think so. Even when I’m calm, if my cousin asks something simple, like about a bill or an appointment, I start going off about the grant, or shipping routes, or my grandmother’s altar. Then I stop and… they don’t seem to know what I meant.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt extremely energetic, irritable, or unusually happy for several days or longer?

Yes… I have times like that. I feel… radiant, like I’ve been chosen for something. It can last days. But if someone questions me or tells me to slow down, I get very angry… like they’re trying to erase me.
Is your thinking usually disorganized like this all the time, or does it only happen sometimes?

It… happens enough that it feels like it’s just how my mind goes. Like I said, my cousin asks about a bill or an appointment, and I’m suddenly explaining the grant, then shipping routes, then my grandmother’s altar. By the time I stop, people look lost.
Do you notice your thinking getting more disorganized when you're feeling extremely energetic or happy?

I’m not sure if it’s more, exactly. It just… happens. Like my cousin asks about a bill or an appointment, and I end up talking about the grant, then shipping routes, then my grandmother’s altar. And then everyone just looks confused.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt extremely sad or depressed for several days or longer?
I… I don’t really know. I have bad days, sure, but I don’t know if I’d call it a whole period like that. It’s hard to separate out.
